JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 18-04-2023 at about 3-45 a.m. the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 03-HU-3453 from Banaswadi main road, IOC Flyover towards Frazer Town, at that time the driver of TATA 407 Tempo bearing No.KA-13-5100 came from Bypanhalli Railway Station towards Mukunda Theatre road near Sevanagar bridge flyover took right U-turn in a rash and negligent manner without giving any indication or horn dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner's, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Specialist Hospital, Kalyan Nagar wherein admitted as an inpatient from 18-04-2023 to 28-04-2023 and then he was shifted to Trust Well Hospital, Bengaluru for better treatment and Neuro Rehabilitation wherein admitted as an inpatient from 28-04-2023 to 02-05-2023 and again admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 02-05- 2023 to 08-05-2023.
So far, the petitioner has spent Rs.14,19,991/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
As per the advice of the doctors, the petitioner is still continuing the follow up treatment.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 26 years.
He was working as Cafe Supervisor at BOLEYAK, Wheeler road Extension, Cooke Town, Bangalore and Mohammed Shariq Khains vs Shashi Kumar

4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1/ R.C. owner of TATA 407 Tempo bearing No.KA-13-5100 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed exparte.

5. Respondent no.2/the insurer of TATA 407 Tempo bearing No.KA-13-5100 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has raised objection regarding inordinate delay on the part of the claimant in filing the claim petition and submitted that the claim petition is barred by limitation, hence, the claim petition cannot be entertained and not maintainable in the eye of law and is liable to be dismissed.

It is further submitted that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the petitioner in collision with the jurisdictional police has created false record and lodged false complaint to get compensation and that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding driving license and the said vehicle was plying without valid permit and FC.

It is further contended that the accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner as he was riding the motorcycle without wearing helmet,
without possessing valid vehicle document and having no knowledge of riding, rode the vehicle in rash a and negligent manner and dashed to the right side fuel tank of the offending vehicle which was moving slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules.
6.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries on account of Road traffic Accident on 18-04-2023 at about 3-45 a.m., near Sevanagar IOC Flyover Bridge, Banasawadi, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of TATA 407 Temple bearing Reg.no.KA-13-5100?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
7. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and examined three witnesses as P.W.2 to PW.4 and marked Ex.P1 to ExP41.

The respondent no.2 has examined its Manager as RW.1 and got marked document as Ex.R1.
8.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 18-04-2023 at about 3-45 a.m. when the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-03-HU-3453 from Banaswadi main road, IOC Flyover towards Frazer Town, at that time the driver of TATA 407 Tempo bearing No.KA-13-5100 (herein after called the offending vehicle)
came from Bypanhalli Railway Station towards Mukunda Theatre road near Sevanagar bridge flyover, took right U-turn in a rash and negligent manner without giving any indication or horn dashed to the motor cycle of the petitioner's, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

The P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 8 and Ex.P19 to 29 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, wound certificate, Motor vehicle Accident report, Mahazar report, order sheet in Misc No.176/2023, Accident report in FIR No.65/2023, permit issued by the Transport Department,
along with Emission Test and Fitness certificate, photographs of petitioner and his vehicle along with CD, order sheet in CC No.22699/2023, plea of the accused, charge sheet, Mahazar, spot sketch,
statement of witnesses, notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon, photographs of the offending vehicle, indemnity bond executed by the owner of the offending vehicle, RC of the offending vehicle and RC card of petitioner's vehicle etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Jibran Khais, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0065/2023 of Banasawadi Traffic Police Station, for the offence punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC.
The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 338 IPC 13.
So far as the objection raised by the respondent no.2 as to delay in filing the claim petition is concerned, it is true that the claim petition is filed after lapse of 68 days.
It is relevant to state here that prior to the filing of claim petition, Mis.,Petition No.176/2023 was filed within 6 months from the date of accident.

The petitioner had filed application u/sec.5 of Limitation Act to condone the delay of 68 days in filing the claim petition and this court vide order dated 31-07-2024 had allowed the said application.
The respondent no.2 has not challenged the said order hence when delay has already been condoned, the question of re-agitating the said issue does not arise.

So far as the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 regarding the negligence contributed by the petitioner is concerned, in order to substantiate the same they have mainly relied upon the IMV report at Ex.P3 wherein it is shown that the right side fuel tank guard of the offending vehicle was damaged and rear silencer, front wheel, mud guard, front fork head light, handle, left Mohammed Shariq Khains vs Shashi Kumar .K.M on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6834372/
4 side crush guard, right side crash guard of the motorcycle of the petitioner was damaged.

sentences.text: It is argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that in order to cause damage to the offending vehicle on its right side fuel tank guard, definitely the petitioner by riding his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner hit to the offending vehicle.
But if the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 22 feet.

The petitioner and the offending vehicle came from same direction but the offending vehicle which came from Bansavadi on the left side of the road took "U" turn towards right side, whereas the petitioner was proceeding on the same line without taking his vehicle either right side or left side.
When offending vehicle was taking right turn they have to have all kind of indication to give proper caution to the other vehicles moving in the said road of his taking U turn.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that the offending vehicle without giving any indication took right U turn of the vehicle.
The respondent no.2 has not examined the driver of the offending vehicle to say that by giving all indication, he took right U turn of the vehicle.

It is quite natural that when offending vehicle took right U turn and the motorcycle was proceeding in the straight road on the right side of the said road and came in contact with the offending vehicle, naturally, the right portion of the offending vehicle and front portion of the motorcycle will get damage.

Hence, the spot mahazar, sketch and IMV report will not come to the aid of the respondents to prove that petitioner was the cause for accident or that along with driver of the offending vehicle even petitioner has also contributed negligence.
It is further relevant to state here that in the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he was in the hospital for quite long time.
If Ex.P19 i.e., the order sheet in CC No.22699/2023 and Ex.
P20 i.e., the plea recorded in the said case, is perused, the driver of the offending vehicle by admitting his guilty has deposited fine amount before the court in the aforesaid case.

It is true that in the judgment relied by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 in ILR 2009 Kar 2921 between Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs., B.C.Kumar & Anr., it was observed that "The M.A.C.T should not and ought not to place sole reliance on the judgment of the Criminal Court while considering the issue of the factum of the accident and the consequent negligence, as stated in the claim petition filed before the Tribunal.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs., B.C.Kumar & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But, the Tribunal will have to assess the evidence before it independently of any finding of the Criminal Court of the question of the driver pleading guilty.
At the most, the circumstance of the driver pleading guilty may be considered as one of the pieces of evidence to support the case of the claimant.

But, the Tribunal should not place implicit reliance only on the circumstance of the driver having pleaded guilty before the Criminal Court and such an approach by the Tribunals will be not only an one sided approach but, at the same time, there is every likelihood of the pleading of guilty by a driver before the Criminal Court having been obtained by adopting various methods so as to ensure that the claimant succeeds before the M.A.C.T. in getting compensation".

14. By relying upon the observation made in the aforesaid judgment, coming to the case in hand, in the present case apart from the accused pleading guilty before the criminal court, the petitioner even has proved the sole negligence contributed by the driver of the offending vehicle by placing spot mahazar, sketch and IMV report.

Even though the learned counsel for respondent no.2 has referred two judgments reported in 2008 ACJ 1188 (SC) and 2018 (1) AKR 152 regarding the contributory negligence but in view of the discussion made herein above this court finds it not just to apply the observation made in the said judgment to the case in hand, because in the present case petitioner has not contributed any Mohammed Shariq Khains vs Shashi Kumar .K.M on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6834372/
5 negligence.

sentences.text: Hence, considering the materials placed on record this court is of the firm opinion that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for accident in which petitioner has not played any role.
Accordingly issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summaries which are at Ex.P2, Ex.P9 to 11.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at Specialist Hospital from 18-04-2023 to 28-04-2023 as inpatient.

Again the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Trustwell Hospitals, Bangalore for two times ie., from 28-04-2023 to 02-05-2023 and from 02-05-2023 to 08-05-2023, in all for a period of 23 days he has taken treatment.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained seven injuries of which injury no.1 to 5 are grievous in nature and injury no.6 and 7 are simple in nature.

16. The petitioner has examined Dr. Bhargav Mundlapudi- consultant at Trilife Hospital (earlier named as Specialist Hospital) as PW.3 and through him case sheet, MLC and police intimation are marked as Ex.P37 to Ex.P39.
The PW3 has given evidence regarding nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner at the time of his admitted to the aforesaid hospital and the nature of treatment given to the PW.1 in detail.

It is deposed by PW.3 that the petitioner has taken treatment in their hospital in ICU and that after 28-04-2023, the petitioner has not taken treatment in their hospital either as inpatient or outpatient.
17.
Dr.Prahlad S T working at Trustwell Hospital, Bangalore is examined as Pw4 and through him Disability certificate and case sheet are marked as Ex.P.40 and Ex.P41.

P.W.4 has deposed that the petitioner was admitted to ICU, evaluated, MRI brain showed multiple hemorrhagic contusions in bilateral cerebral hemispheres with features of diffuse axonal/vascular injury, thin subdural collection in the left fronto temporal and posterios aspect of flax, postoperative changes in the right temporal lobe.
Cardiologist opinion sought and advice followed.

He was treated with IV antibiotics,
antiepileptics, antiedema and other supportive medications.

Plastic surgery opinion sought for left lower limb injury and managed accordingly, Endotracheal C/s showed klebsiella growth for which antibiotics were adjusted accordingly the petitioner, was discharged from ICU and was shifted to ward for neurorehabilitation.
Under aseptic precautions tracheostomy tube was removed and reinserted on 04-05- 2023.
Dr. Jithendra (plastic surgeon) opinion was sought, dressing was done and below knee slab was removed.
On 07-05-2023 tracheostomy closure was done.
Tolerated procedure well.
Daily physiotherapy was done.
During stay vitals were regularly monitored and managed appropriately.

18. PW.4 further deposed that petitioner was discharged on 08-05-2023 in conscious state with commands to obey, ambulating with support on RT and Oral Feeds and get physiotherapy with discharge medication.
19. PW.4 further deposed that the petitioner is on regular follow up and was last evaluated by him on 16-06- 2025.

According to the gazette of India extra ordinary part II section 3 subsection ii dated January 5 2018, the petitioner is having 43% disability including head, brain, upper limb, lower limb and IDEAS scoring.

sentences.text: The Learned counsel for respondent no.2 submitted that petitioner has examined non treated doctor as PW.4 and it is the non treated doctor who has assessed the disability of the petitioner.

By disputing the medical bills ie., Ex.P12 it is submitted by the Learned counsel for respondent no.2 that in the Ex.P12, the employee name and ID number is mentioned hence the medical bills are paid by the employer as petitioner has availed medical reimbursement facility from the employer, hence medical bills produced by the petitioner cannot be considered.

21. If the evidence of PW.3 and 4 and medical documents are perused, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his head and other parts of the body and he undergone surgeries and spent huge amount for treatment.
If the evidence of PW.3 and PW.4 are perused, they are the treated doctors and PW.4 being the treated doctor has assessed the disability at 43%.
It is relevant to state here that petitioner has independently appeared before the court and given evidence.
As observed by this court, in almost all the hearing dates the petitioner marked his presence before the court.

Hence,
there is no reason to believe the version made in the claim petition that petitioner is bed ridden.
Hence, by considering the evidence given by the PW.4 and the present position of the petitioner, this court inclines to consider the disability of petitioner at 35% .
22. Considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
23. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained five grievous injuries.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards pain and suffering.

24. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are concerned, he has produced Specialist Hospital IP consolidated Final Bill for Rs. 9,65,000/-, Trustwell Hospitals Bill of supply for Rs.89,140/- and Rs.1,48,659/-, medical bills for Rs.2,17,200/- at Ex.P12 and in all incurred sum of Rs.14,19,999/-.
To evidence the fact that the family of the petitioner had paid the bill amount, the petitioner has examined his brother as PW.2.
The Pw.2 has produced his bank statement as per Ex.P33 and 34 to prove that payments were made through account.

Hence, there is every reason to believe that petitioner had incurred sum of Rs.14,19,999/- towards medical expenses and entire medical expenses was met by the family members of the petitioner but not by his employer.

Hence,
petitioner is entitled for medical expenses to the tune of Rs.14,19,999/-.
25.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 26 years and he was working as Cafe Supervisor at BOLEYAK, Wheeler Road Extension, Cooke Town, Bangalore and drawing salary of Rs.35,000/- per month.

The petitioner has produced employment letter issued by Coffee Works, Registration certificate of M/s Coffee works along with certificate u/Sec.63 of BSA 2023 and Bank statement at Ex.P13, Ex.P31 and Ex.P32.
26.

It is vehemently argued by the Learned counsel for respondent no.2 that even though petitioner has produced the aforesaid documents but he has not examined the author of Ex.P13, hence the income of the petitioner cannot be considered as Rs.35,000/- and to take the notional income.

sentences.text: In the light of the argument canvassed by the Learned counsel for respondent no.2 if the Ex.P13 is perused, it is the certificate issued by one Emad Ahmed from Coffee work, where by certified that petitioner is working in the said Coffee work from October 2021 to April -2023 as Cafe Supervisor and from April 2023 he is not working in the said Cafe.
If Ex.P32 is perused, there is no entry regarding transfer of sum of Rs.35,000/- every month from Coffee work towards the salary of the petitioner.

Hence, as rightly argued by the Learned counsel for respondent no.2, when there is no authenticated document to prove the monthly income of the petitioner, the court cannot consider the monthly income of the petitioner as Rs.35,000/- per month.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence considers the monthly income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
28.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 23 days as inpatient in Specialist Hospital and Trust Well Hospital, Bangalore.

sentences.text: Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 6 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,000/- p.m. for six months.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.96,000/-
(Rs.16,000X6) towards loss of income during the laid down period .
29. From the evidence of Pw3 and 4 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Specialist Hospital, and Trust Well Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further for 23 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.60,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2023.
30.
The petitioner has contended that he is aged about 26 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P18/Aadhaar card of the petitioner which shows his date of birth as 02-03-1997 that means he was aged about 26 years.
Hence considering the Notarized copy of the Aadhaar card this court has taken the age of petitioner as 26 years.

31. So taking in to consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,000/- p.m. and by considering the evidence of PW.2 as he has assessed disability on little higher side, this court inclines to take the disability on whole body at 35% and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 26 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age of 26-30 is '17'.
So by applying the multiplier '17' the future loss of income due to disability would comes to Rs.11,42,400/- (i.e., Rs.16,000 x35% x 17 x12 )-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.11,42,400/- towards future loss of income due to disability.

The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:

Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.28,68,399/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakh Sixty Eight Thousand Three Hundred Ninety Nine only).
32.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
33. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.28,68,399/- + cost of Rs.1,250/- imposed vide order on IA No.III, VII & VIII.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.28,69,649/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakh Sixty Nine Thousand Six Hundred Forty Nine only).
A Sum of Rs.28,68,399/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
The respondent no.2 has raised objection regarding inordinate delay on the part of the claimant in filing the claim petition and submitted that the claim petition is barred by limitation, hence, the claim petition cannot be entertained and not maintainable in the eye of law and is liable to be dismissed.
On the basis of the complaint lodged by Jibran Khais, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0065/2023 of Banasawadi Traffic Police Station, for the offence punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries on account of Road traffic Accident on 18-04-2023 at about 3-45 a.m., near Sevanagar IOC Flyover Bridge, Banasawadi, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of TATA 407 Temple bearing Reg.no.KA-13-5100?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 338 IPC 13.
The petitioner had filed application u/sec.5 of Limitation Act to condone the delay of 68 days in filing the claim petition and this court vide order dated 31-07-2024 had allowed the said application.
The respondent no.2 has not challenged the said order hence when delay has already been condoned, the question of re-agitating the said issue does not arise.
The respondent no.2 has not examined the driver of the offending vehicle to say that by giving all indication, he took right U turn of the vehicle.
It is quite natural that when offending vehicle took right U turn and the motorcycle was proceeding in the straight road on the right side of the said road and came in contact with the offending vehicle, naturally, the right portion of the offending vehicle and front portion of the motorcycle will get damage.
Hence, the spot mahazar, sketch and IMV report will not come to the aid of the respondents to prove that petitioner was the cause for accident or that along with driver of the offending vehicle even petitioner has also contributed negligence.
Hence, considering the materials placed on record this court is of the firm opinion that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for accident in which petitioner has not played any role.
22. Considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken, this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
23. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained five grievous injuries.
Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards pain and suffering.
If Ex.P32 is perused, there is no entry regarding transfer of sum of Rs.35,000/- every month from Coffee work towards the salary of the petitioner.
Hence taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,000/- p.m. for six months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.96,000/-
(Rs.16,000X6) towards loss of income during the laid down period .
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The petitioner and the offending vehicle came from same direction but the offending vehicle which came from Bansavadi on the left side of the road took "U" turn towards right side, whereas the petitioner was proceeding on the same line without taking his vehicle either right side or left side.
When offending vehicle was taking right turn they have to have all kind of indication to give proper caution to the other vehicles moving in the said road of his taking U turn.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that the offending vehicle without giving any indication took right U turn of the vehicle.
Hence, as rightly argued by the Learned counsel for respondent no.2, when there is no authenticated document to prove the monthly income of the petitioner, the court cannot consider the monthly income of the petitioner as Rs.35,000/- per month.
Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence considers the monthly income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
28.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 23 days as inpatient in Specialist Hospital and Trust Well Hospital, Bangalore.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 6 months as complete laid down period.
opennyai_summary.decision:
So by applying the multiplier '17' the future loss of income due to disability would comes to Rs.11,42,400/- (i.e., Rs.16,000 x35% x 17 x12 )-.
Hence this Tribunal holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.11,42,400/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
Sl.No Heads Amount Rs.
1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 1,50,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs. 14,19,999/-
Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 60,000/-
 charges and nourishing food 5.
Future loss of income Rs. 11,42,400/-
 Total Rs.28,68,399/-
Therefore, this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.28,68,399/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakh Sixty Eight Thousand Three Hundred Ninety Nine only).
32.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
33. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.28,68,399/- + cost of Rs.1,250/- imposed vide order on IA No.III, VII & VIII.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.28,69,649/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakh Sixty Nine Thousand Six Hundred Forty Nine only).
A Sum of Rs.28,68,399/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit of the said amount and interest, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
